sentences.text:
This Misc. Appeal was admitted for final hearing and reserved for orders on 27/02/2025.
2.

This appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant/non-applicant (owner and driver of the offending vehicle) against the award dated 24/07/2024 passed in MACC No.169 of 2021 (Heeralal Kushwaha & others vs. Moolchandra Jaiswal) whereby learned Fifth Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Waidhan District Singrauli has awarded compensation of Rs.8,62,400/- for a motor accident dated 10/06/2021 on account of death of Urmila Kushwaha.

sentences.text: 3. The present appeal has been filed on the ground that on 10/06/2021 i.e. the day mentioned in the claim application, appellant was not present at the place of incident, in fact, he was admitted in Bansal Hospital, Bhopal.

4. At the time of arguments, learned counsel for the appellant very fairly admitted that although documents of treatment were filed but did not call the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:20715 2 MA-7401-2024 original relevant record along with the staff of the Hospital to verify the documents of treatment.
Whereas, learned counsel for the respondents submitted that appellant has miserably failed to prove the plea of alibi as the sole burden lies on him to prove the same.

5. Perused the award, pleadings and evidence.

6. On perusal of the record it seems that the sole ground of appeal pressed by way of arguments at the time of hearing was regarding the plea of alibi that applicant was not present on the spot but it is seen that charge-sheet has been filed against the appellant/owner of the vehicle.
Appellant did not call the Investigating Officer to establish that wrong charge-sheet has been filed.
The appellant Moolchandra has been arrested and FIR No.364/2021 under Section 304-A of IPC has been registered against him.
There is nothing on record that FIR or charge-sheet was quashed at the behest of the appellant herein.

7. Considering the pleading and evidence of both the parties and looking to the statements of Vishithmuni Kushwaha (applicant witness No.1), Ramlalit Kushwaha (Applicant witness No.2), and evidence of Rambahadur Kushwaha (Applicant witness No.3), alibi of the appellant is not proved.
It is seen that evidence of the applicant was closed on 21/05/2024 and thereafter, case was fixed for non-applicant evidence.
On 29/05/2024 documents were filed by non-applicant and he has examined himself.
8. The date of incident in this case is 10/06/2021.

In para-1, the non- applicant submitted that on 09/06/2021 he was at his home, therefore it is not a case that he is stating that on 10/06/2021 i.e.
the date of accident and at the relevant time, he was admitted in the Hospital.
In fact, in his evidence he has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:20715 3 MA-7401-2024 not exhibited any particular document to prove his plea of alibi.
Same is the case of non-applicant witness No.2 who again stated that on 10/06/2021 Moolchandra was at his home.

No specific document is exhibited,
therefore over all defence of the appellant that defence of the appellant regarding alibi is not proved and the award of the Tribunal is well justified.
9. Hence, appeal is having no merits and is hereby dismissed.
(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE mc
